title: a `neural_block` descriptor's `forward_exec.kind` outside the exec-ref vocabulary is rejected
why: An exec reference's `kind` is a schema DISCRIMINANT:
it names HOW the reference must be read, so an unrecognized value is refused rather
than dispatched on as though it were an ordinary `{'kind': 'kernel', ...}` object.
v1 has exactly one legal kind ('kernel'); a future aggregate/plan-bundle kind would
RESHAPE the object (a digest payload alongside `kind`), which is a meaning change and
therefore a `schema_version` bump, never a silent new value an old loader might
The rejected value is a deliberately inert placeholder ('not_a_registered_exec_kind'),
the same convention row02's unknown `pattern` uses: naming a real future kind here
would be a scope breach, since admitting one is its own governed schema event.
Fixture content is row01's golden with one field changed (`forward_exec.kind` only —
`forward_exec.kernel` and the untouched `vjp_exec` stay valid), so the ONLY thing that
can make it reject is the discriminant under test. The exec-ref fields are checked in
SORTED order in both languages, and `forward_exec` sorts before `vjp_exec`, so this
row also pins which field fires first on a descriptor whose exec refs disagree.
`host_add_plugin` is exercised too: its only structural gate is the shared validator,
so the check must live there, not in a per-loader afterthought.
